Generate A Polynomial Pools Matrix

Source: R/pp_matrix.R
pp_matrix.Rd

Construct a binary pooling matrix by the Polynomial Pools (PP) algorithm, using polynomial evaluation over \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\) to define the pool incidence pattern.

Usage

pp_matrix(q, d, nl, N = NULL)

Arguments

q

Integer scalar giving the Galois-field order. It must be a prime power so that \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\) exists. This parameter controls the number of pools per layer and the coordinate alphabet used by the PP construction.

d

Integer scalar giving the PP dimension. It must satisfy \(d \ge 2\). The full untruncated design has \(N_{\max} = q^d\) individuals and canonical pool size \(q^{d-1}\).

nl

Integer scalar giving the number of layers, written \(n_l\) in the PP literature. It must satisfy \(1 \le n_l \le q + 1\). The returned design has \(J = n_l q\) pools and each individual is assigned to exactly \(n_l\) pools.

N

Integer scalar giving the number of individuals actually retained in the matrix. The default is \(N = q^d\). It must satisfy \(1 \le N \le q^d\) and \(q \mid N\). Values smaller than \(q^d\) truncate the full PP design to its first \(N\) columns.

Value

A sparse binary matrix of class dgCMatrix with dimensions \(J \times N\), where \(J = n_l q\). Entry \(M_{ji} = 1\) indicates that individual \(i\) belongs to pool \(j\). The matrix carries attribute "pp" containing a named list with:

q

Integer; field order

d

Integer; dimension

nl

Integer; number of layers

N

Integer; number of samples

M

Integer; legacy display alias for the number of pools \(J\)

pool_size

Integer; actual number of samples per pool (first row-sum after any \(N < q^d\) truncation; equals \(q^{d-1}\) only when \(N = q^d\))

k_max

Integer; maximum detectable positives with COMP

In the full untruncated design, all column sums equal \(n_l\) and all row sums equal \(q^{d-1}\). Under truncation, the column sums remain \(w_i = |\mathcal{J}_i| = n_l\), while the row sums may differ slightly from \(q^{d-1}\) near the truncation boundary.

Details

Let \(\mathbf{M} = (M_{ji}) \in \{0,1\}^{J \times N}\) denote the returned pooling matrix, where \(j \in \{1, \ldots, J\}\) indexes pools and \(i \in \{1, \ldots, N\}\) indexes individuals. The PP construction uses polynomial evaluation over \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\). The main derived quantities are $$N_{\max} = q^d, \qquad J = n_l q, \qquad k_{\max} = \left\lfloor \frac{n_l - 1}{d - 1} \right\rfloor.$$

Individuals are indexed by field-valued coordinates and assigned to pools by polynomial relations over \(\mathrm{GF}(q)\). In the full untruncated design, each individual appears in exactly \(n_l\) pools, each pool contains exactly \(q^{d-1}\) individuals, and any two individuals share at most \(d - 1\) pools.

When \(N < q^d\), the constructor truncates the full design to its first \(N\) columns. The column weights remain \(w_i = |\mathcal{J}_i| = n_l\), while row sizes may vary slightly near the truncation boundary.

The standard PP-based P-BEST matrix family uses \(q = 8\), \(d = 3\), \(n_l = 6\), and \(N = 384\), giving \(J = 48\) pools and \(k_{\max} = 2\) under the PP COMP detection bound.

Long derivations and family context are developed in the package vignettes, especially ppgt_pp and ppgt_pbest.

PP Structure

In the full untruncated design, all column sums equal \(n_l\) and all row sums equal \(q^{d-1}\). Pools within each layer are disjoint, and the intersection bound implies that COMP can separate negatives whenever the number of positives stays below the PP detection limit.

P-BEST Context

The package documentation uses the term "PP-based P-BEST" for the \(q = 8\), \(d = 3\), \(n_l = 6\), \(N = 384\) matrix family. That matrix family is distinct from later package-specific clinical helpers and should not be read as a blanket claim about every P-BEST protocol layer.

References

Tan, Y. H. I. (2020). Pooling matrix designs for group testing. SIAM Undergraduate Research Online, 13, 1-21.

Shental, N., Levy, S., Wuvshet, V., et al. (2020). Efficient high-throughput SARS-CoV-2 testing to detect asymptomatic carriers. Science Advances, 6(37), eabc5961.

Brust, D., & Brust, J. J. (2023). Effective matrix designs for COVID-19 group testing. BMC Bioinformatics, 24, Article 26.

See also

gf, pp_decode, pp_design, pp_verify

Other polynomial_pools: polynomial_pools, pp_design(), pp_verify()

Examples

# P-BEST standard design: 48 pools x 384 samples
M_pbest <- pp_matrix(q = 8, d = 3, nl = 6, N = 384)
M_pbest
